body.statement: Let \(n\geq 1\), let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open, and let \(F:U\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable.  If \(DF(x_0)\) is invertible at \(x_0\in U\), then there are open neighborhoods \(U_0\) of \(x_0\) and \(W_0\) of \(F(x_0)\) such that \(F|_{U_0}:U_0\to W_0\) is one-to-one and onto and has a continuously differentiable inverse.

attestation.note: The emitted claim is the local-diffeomorphism conclusion of the cited inverse-function theorem; the bibliography key, theorem locator, and a stable complete-text URL are supplied.
